claims: Temporary Protected Status (TPS) is a U.S. immigration benefit granted by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to eligible nationals of designated countries facing ongoing armed conflict, environmental disasters, or extraordinary, temporary conditions.
TPS allows beneficiaries to live and work in the U.S. legally for a limited time.
TPS holders receive temporary protection from removal.
TPS holders receive work authorization (Employment Authorization Document).
TPS applicants must be from a designated country.
TPS applicants must have been continuously physically present in the U.S. since the designated date.
TPS applicants must file during the registration period.
TPS does not automatically lead to lawful permanent residence (a "green card").
TPS does not automatically lead to citizenship.
As of early 2026, countries with TPS include Afghanistan, Cameroon, El Salvador, Haiti, Honduras, Nepal, Nicaragua, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Ukraine, Venezuela, and others.
Individuals can apply for TPS using Form I-821.
Form I-821 is the Application for Temporary Protected Status.
TPS applications are submitted through USCIS.
